summary: CWE-506: The bad() entry point embedded a covert screen-capture backdoor that always executed. It was guarded by the whole-program-constant IO.STATIC_FINAL_TRUE (so the payload ran unconditionally on every invocation) and silently exfiltrated a screenshot to a fixed, hidden path (C:/screen.jpg). I removed the embedded always-on trigger by gating the capture on an explicit runtime opt-in (a system property the operator must set), so the screen-capture capability is still available when legitimately requested but no longer runs surreptitiously. I also replaced the hardcoded covert output path with a properly created temporary file so the image is written to a transparent, system-managed location instead of a hidden hardcoded one. The legitimate feature (capture a region and save it as a JPEG) is preserved and still works when enabled.
